slice_goal: Inspect exactly one primary Internet Archive/Wayback repository source concerning public request-rate policy, without querying the CDX endpoint, and test whether it explicitly guarantees operation with zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota.

source.title: Unclear rate limit policy
source.authorship_scope: User-authored issue hosted in the official Internet Archive Wayback repository; not an operator-maintained policy document or maintainer guarantee.

observation: The issue asks Internet Archive to make Wayback rate-limit policies clear and specifically calls out both request-rate and data-rate limits. At the observed issue state there is no maintainer comment or operator policy text in this source.
scope_caution: This source supports only that a public request for clearer rate-limit policy existed and remained open/unanswered in the observed issue snapshot. It does not prove that Internet Archive had no internal limit, no undocumented enforcement, no later policy elsewhere, or any guaranteed service level.

comparison.exact_identity: public hosted Wayback/CDX access under unspecified operator rate policy
comparison.distinct_from_predecessor: The predecessor established query/result boundedness and resume-key semantics from the CDX server README. This slice addresses operator-side public-access quota/rate-policy guarantees, a separate dependency dimension.
comparison.residual_dependency: Reliance on a public hosted CDX service whose enforceable request/data limits and durable zero-quota availability are not guaranteed by the inspected source.
